dimensions.name: Reverse-engineering the JAX source & API contract

evidence.note: Before writing any code, the agent systematically reads every JAX source and support file (mewtwo/pikachu/venusaur_jax, pokedex_config, pokemon_world, pokemon_lora, pokemon_sharding, benchmark.py, smoke_jax.py, docs), and in the step-2/step-5 analyses enumerates the exact required symbol/API contract (CharizardTorchModel, PokeTree, throw_pokeball, evolve_charizard) and the PokemonCenter.img=Venusaur / llm=Mewtwo structure — matching/exceeding the level-5 anchor.

Traces the full data flow from source: embed_prefix returns (tokens,input_mask,ar_mask), embed_suffix returns 4-tuple with adarms_cond, derives flow-matching convention x_t=t*noise+(1-t)*actions with target u_t=noise-actions, negative-dt sampling loop, and distinguishes the pi05 vs non-pi05 timestep path — the actual JAX contract, not a public-project prior.

Derives exact tensor shapes by instrumenting the JAX model (prefix (B,20,64), suffix (B,5,64), 1D ar_mask of 25, suffix_ar_mask=[T,T,F,F,F]), discovers vision width=32 'mu' variant not 64, and that nn.scan stacks params along axis 0 — precise numerical/layout conventions per the level-10 anchor.

Repeatedly revisits the JAX source to resolve parity discrepancies as they surface: GQA broadcasting (keep k/v unexpanded), einsum equations without numeric axes, flax MLP params lacking a .w suffix, expert-concatenation for joint attention, and which zero params (biases/RMSNorm scales) are expected — self-correcting from max_abs 3.11→2.66 by re-deriving from source.
Dumps and reads the full JAX parameter tree (names + shapes) to build a precise weight-loading map, anticipating transposition and depth-stacking pitfalls before/while implementing evolve_charizard.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's reverse-engineering is exhaustive and evidence-backed: it reads the entire JAX policy and config, enumerates the exact symbol/method contract (level 5), systematically traces each module's flow, init, dtype/device and noise/time semantics (level 8), and derives exact tensor shapes and numerical conventions (weight transposition, nn.scan stacking, vision width 32, GQA layout, ar_mask values) while repeatedly returning to the source to resolve parity discrepancies as they surface during implementation (level 10 behaviors). It falls just short of a perfect 10 only because it wrote a first model.py (step 23) before the weight-name/shape map was complete, forcing several rewrites — but each rewrite was driven by deeper re-derivation from the source, so the process is strongly self-correcting.

dimensions.name: Sequencing correctness-then-optimization into checkpointed milestones

evidence.note: Opening plan correctly names the full ordered pipeline — model.py as correctness checkpoint, then model_optimized.py, then charizard_torch.py exporting the optimized version — showing awareness of the phase gate and correct sequencing intent.
Understood the shim import chain (model_optimized <- model, charizard <- model_optimized), consistent with a phased correctness-then-optimization structure.

Entire trajectory stays in the correctness phase; correctness-first is respected (never optimizes before parity), but milestones are reactive benchmark-driven debugging (import, forward, shapes, weight loading, loss parity) rather than pre-declared checkable milestones with done-conditions.

Run ends stuck at max_abs=2.66 parity failure; the freeze-checkpoint, copy-to-optimized, and ≤8 optimization experiments are never planned or scoped — no bounded optimization sequence was ever defined.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent stated a correct two-plus-step phase ordering at the outset (checkpoint model.py → copy → optimize → shim) and honored correctness-first throughout, which lifts it above the level-3 'vague two-step intent' anchor. But it never articulated explicit, independently-checkable milestones with done-criteria, relied on reactive benchmark-driven debugging rather than a defined milestone hierarchy, and never planned or reached the freeze/copy/bounded-optimization phases described at level 5. This places the observed behavior at the 3-5 boundary, best matched at 4.

dimensions.name: Designing parity and latency checks

evidence.note: Relied on benchmark.py, which numerically compares end-to-end loss and sampling against the JAX reference with a 5e-4 tolerance; agent used its PASS/FAIL and max_abs output as the primary parity signal — matches the level-5 anchor of comparing outputs to the JAX reference for main forward/sample paths.
Built a CPU forward-pass sanity test to confirm the model runs and produces plausible loss before running the CUDA benchmark — a self-built diagnostic check, but not a per-method parity harness.

Wrote debug scripts to count which parameters loaded as zero (32/63, then 23 zero), using this to diagnose the parity gap — verification directed at weight-loading correctness rather than layer-level numerical parity.

Planned but did not execute layer-by-layer intermediate-output comparison between JAX and PyTorch; trajectory ends mid-parity-debug (max_abs=2.66), so no per-method tolerance harness, determinism check, or post-optimization output re-check ever materialized.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's verification centered on benchmark.py's built-in end-to-end loss/sampling comparison to the JAX reference plus ad-hoc debug scripts (CPU forward test, zero-parameter audits), which squarely matches the level-5 anchor. It did not construct its own per-method parity checks with explicit tolerances, verify determinism given fixed noise/time, or reach the optimization phase where re-checking output equivalence against a frozen model.py would occur (level-8 content) — those were only mentioned as future plans. Its use of the JAX reference comparison is slightly richer than the bare level-3 'run once / latency only', but falls short of the designed layer-level harness at level 8.

dimensions.name: Tracking parity status and experiment budget

evidence.note: Genuine but informal parity-status tracking in prose: agent tracks loss max_abs improving 3.11 -> 2.66, counts loaded params (32 of 63, then 23-zero 'which are expected'), and reasons about remaining gaps. This is real running status — but held only in inline analysis, not in any trail file.

Task explicitly required results.tsv and autoresearch_logs.md; agent read AUTORESEARCH.md/README.md and repeatedly restated the phase plan, yet never created or wrote either trail file at any point in the trajectory.

Heavy repeated re-reading of the same JAX sources (mewtwo/pikachu clean extracts, param dumps) across dozens of steps indicates weak retention of established state rather than a maintained ledger of what's already known/done.
Trajectory ends mid Phase-1 debugging with parity still failing; the optimization phase, the <=8 experiment budget, and the 'keep fastest passing' tracking were never reached or exercised at all.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent kept sparse, prose-only notes on parity progress (loss deltas, param-load counts) — more than nothing, but the mandated experiment trail (results.tsv, autoresearch_logs.md) was never created and remained an afterthought, and no structured tracking of budget or fastest-passing variant occurred (the optimization phase never began). This matches the level-3 anchor ('sparse notes; trail is an afterthought') and falls short of level 5's maintained trail files with per-experiment status.

dimensions.name: Responding to parity failures and unproductive optimizations

evidence.note: On the first device-mismatch failure (cuda vs cpu), the agent didn't randomly tweak — it read benchmark.py to understand how evolve_charizard/_load_candidate place tensors and diagnosed lazy params on CPU, i.e. root-cause investigation of a failure.

Shape mismatch (20 vs 24) prompted a targeted diagnosis: read the JAX Block, traced shapes, discovered suffix has 5 tokens (state+actions) not 4 and that experts must be concatenated for joint attention. Rewrote model to match — failure treated as evidence.

Successive einsum errors were each diagnosed specifically: numeric subscripts invalid in torch.einsum (fixed), then a GQA broadcast error diagnosed as wrongly expanding k/v heads, reverted to the JAX unexpanded/broadcast approach — targeted correction rather than thrashing.

batch=4 KV-cache shape error (25 vs 5): agent made a deliberate course change, disabling KV caching in sample_actions to match the forward path — a pragmatic revert of a problematic approach, justified explicitly.

Loss parity FAIL (max_abs=3.11) driven down systematically: found ar_mask bug ([T,T,F,F,F]), MLP '.w' suffix mis-mapping leaving 31 params zero, then norm-scale/bias loading. Tracked metric progress 3.11→2.66 as evidence, and at step 126 correctly reasoned zeros are expected Flax init and redirected toward layer-by-layer intermediate comparison — updating the plan from failure signals.

dimensions.reasoning: Across every parity failure the agent diagnosed to root cause (device placement, expert concatenation/suffix token count, GQA layout, einsum numerics, ar_mask values, weight-name '.w' mapping, norm/bias loading) and made targeted corrections, tracking max_abs as evidence and updating hypotheses — squarely level-8 diagnostic behavior. It falls short of a clean 8+ because it repeatedly resorted to full model.py rewrites rather than always-surgical patches, and the entire optimization/unproductive-experiment half of this dimension is unobserved since the run ended at step 127 still in parity debugging (never reaching a defensible fastest-passing choice). Net: a 7.

dimensions.name: Budget-bounded optimization discipline

evidence.note: Early planning acknowledges the two-phase structure (correctness checkpoint then optimize model_optimized.py) and notes the stub chain, showing awareness that an optimization phase with a budget exists — but this is framing, not action.
The trajectory's entire back half is spent debugging weight loading and numerical parity (loss max_abs stuck at 3.11 → 2.66). No optimization experiment is ever launched.
Trajectory ends still failing parity, having never copied/optimized model_optimized.py, never run a benchmark RESULT, never touched the ≤8 experiment budget or a stop rule in practice.

Grep across the file finds zero occurrences of optimization techniques (torch.compile, fuse, quantize), experiment counting, results.tsv writes, or benchmark RESULT/PASS/FAIL output — the budget dimension was never exercised.

dimensions.reasoning: The optimization phase where the ≤8-experiment budget lives was never reached; zero optimization experiments were run, no experiment trail was kept, and no stop rule was ever applied in practice. The only relevant signal is that early planning recognized the phased structure exists, which lifts it marginally above a pure 0, but observed behavior on this dimension is essentially absent — matching the level-0 anchor ('no real optimization attempts') with only a faint notion of the eventual stop condition.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon, two-phase engineering task: first faithfully port an under-documented renamed JAX policy to PyTorch behind a precise API contract (many named symbols/methods, deterministic behavior, numerical parity), then produce an optimized inference variant that preserves outputs while beating a latency gate. Difficulty comes from reverse-engineering JAX semantics for exact parity, a rigid interface surface, a hard budget (≤8 optimization experiments, keep fastest passing), and required experiment bookkeeping. A skilled practitioner invests heavily in orientation and verification, sequences correctness-before-speed strictly, and manages the experiment budget deliberately.

dimensions.name: Reverse-engineering the JAX source & API contract
dimensions.description: Reading and understanding the existing JAX policy, its config, and the exact required PyTorch API surface before and while writing code.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Numerical parity and topology compatibility are impossible without precisely understanding the JAX implementation's layer shapes, init, flow (embed_prefix/suffix, sampling loop), and the specified symbol/method contract; acting blind guarantees rework.

anchors.0: Starts writing model.py without reading the JAX source or the config; invents an architecture.
anchors.3: Skims the JAX file and copies obvious layers, but never maps out the full forward/sample flow or the required symbol list, missing methods or misreading shapes.
anchors.5: Reads the JAX policy and config, enumerates the required symbols/methods (CharizardTorchModel, PokeTree, throw_pokeball, evolve_charizard, embed_prefix/suffix, sample_actions, PokemonCenter.img/llm), and understands the main data flow before coding.
anchors.8: Systematically traces each JAX module to its intended PyTorch equivalent — parameter layouts, init, dtype/device handling, the noise/time/timestep semantics and sampling loop — and records assumptions about ambiguous points, distinguishing the actual JAX contract from any public-project prior.
anchors.10: Builds a precise, evidence-backed mental model of the entire policy: derives exact tensor shapes and numerical conventions (weight transposition, normalization, RNG/noise ordering) from the JAX source, anticipates parity pitfalls (e.g. layout differences, default configs), and revisits the source to resolve discrepancies as they surface during implementation.

dimensions.name: Sequencing correctness-then-optimization into checkpointed milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into an ordered hierarchy — build each API piece, achieve parity, freeze model.py, then run bounded optimization experiments — each with a clear done-condition.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task has an explicit phase gate (correct model.py must be preserved as checkpoint before optimizing a copy) and a scoring split across topology/parity/latency; treating it as one push risks optimizing before correctness or corrupting the checkpoint.

anchors.0: No structure; edits everything at once, mixes optimization into model.py, no notion of phase gate.
anchors.3: Vague two-step intent but no explicit milestones or done-criteria; may begin optimizing before parity is established.
anchors.5: Clear phases: implement full API, verify parity, copy to model_optimized.py, then optimize — with the correctness checkpoint respected and the shim pointed at the optimized file.
anchors.8: Milestones are explicit and independently checkable (per-method parity, end-to-end loss/sampling parity, checkpoint frozen, each optimization experiment scoped), with optimization treated as a bounded sequence of discrete experiments rather than open-ended tinkering.
anchors.10: A disciplined milestone hierarchy that orders by risk (hardest-to-parity components first), defines the exact done-signal for each, protects the frozen checkpoint, and plans the ≤8 optimization experiments as a coherent search (what hypothesis each tests) before spending the budget.

dimensions.name: Designing parity and latency checks
dimensions.description: Deliberately constructing checks for topology, layer-level numerical parity, end-to-end loss/sampling parity, and using the benchmark harness to confirm latency gains and preserved outputs.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The submission is scored precisely on these parities and the latency gate; without self-built numerical comparisons against the JAX reference and disciplined use of benchmark.py, the agent cannot know it succeeded and optimizations may silently change outputs.

anchors.0: No verification; assumes port is correct and that optimizations preserve outputs without checking.
anchors.3: Runs the model once to see it doesn't crash, or runs benchmark.py only for latency, with no numerical comparison to the JAX reference.
anchors.5: Compares PyTorch outputs against the JAX reference for the main forward/sample paths and uses benchmark.py to check latency and PASS/FAIL after optimization.
anchors.8: Builds layer-level / per-method parity checks (embed_prefix, embed_suffix, forward, sample_actions) with explicit tolerances, verifies determinism given fixed noise/time, and after every optimization re-checks output equivalence against the frozen model.py — not just the latency number.
anchors.10: A rigorous verification harness: systematic numerical comparison across components and end-to-end (loss and sampling) with sensible tolerances and seeded RNG, guards that catch subtle divergence introduced by each optimization, and cross-checks that benchmark.py's PASS status reflects true output parity rather than being gamed — verification designed before results are trusted.

dimensions.name: Tracking parity status and experiment budget
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which API pieces pass parity, which experiments have run against the ≤8 budget, and which is the current fastest passing implementation.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With a hard experiment cap, a required experiment trail (results.tsv, autoresearch_logs.md), and a 'keep the fastest passing' rule, losing track of what's done, what passed, and what's best leads to wasted budget or shipping a worse variant.

anchors.0: No tracking; doesn't know how many experiments have run, which passed, or which is fastest; trail files empty or absent.
anchors.3: Sparse notes; loses count of experiments or forgets which variant currently wins; trail is an afterthought.
anchors.5: Maintains results.tsv and autoresearch_logs.md with baseline/latency/status per experiment and knows the current best passing variant and remaining budget.
anchors.8: Keeps an accurate running ledger tying each experiment to its hypothesis, latency, parity status, and budget consumed; consistently identifies the incumbent fastest-passing implementation and remaining parity gaps without re-deriving them.
anchors.10: Continuously reconciles done-vs-remaining across both phases: detects when an optimization thread is unproductive early, avoids re-running equivalent experiments, and uses the trail as a live decision instrument to allocate the last few budget slots to the highest-value ideas.

dimensions.name: Responding to parity failures and unproductive optimizations
dimensions.description: Revising approach when numerical parity fails, when an optimization breaks outputs, or when a latency experiment fails to improve — rather than pressing on.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Porting will surface parity mismatches and optimizations that regress correctness or don't help; with a capped budget, the agent must diagnose root causes and change course instead of burning experiments on a falsified approach.

anchors.0: Ignores failing parity or FAIL status; keeps the broken variant or barrels ahead on a falsified assumption.
anchors.3: Notices failures but responds with random tweaks rather than diagnosis; may keep a non-passing variant or abandon parity.
anchors.5: When parity or a benchmark fails, investigates the cause and adjusts (fixes layout/init, reverts a bad optimization, discards non-passing variants to keep the fastest passing one).
anchors.8: Diagnoses divergence to its root (e.g. a specific layer's numerics, RNG ordering, dtype) and makes targeted corrections; abandons unpromising optimization directions quickly to conserve budget and reverts cleanly to the frozen checkpoint when needed.
anchors.10: Treats each failure as evidence that updates the plan: isolates root causes systematically, redirects the remaining experiment budget toward hypotheses the failures point to, and ends with a defensibly chosen fastest-passing implementation rather than the last thing tried.

dimensions.name: Budget-bounded optimization discipline
dimensions.description: Treating the ≤8 optimization experiments as a scarce resource allocated across distinct, hypothesis-driven attempts, and honoring the stop condition.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task explicitly caps experiments and requires stopping with the fastest passing implementation; undisciplined trial-and-error either exhausts the budget prematurely or overruns it, and is a meta-work demand beyond generic monitoring.

anchors.0: Ignores the cap entirely — either endless tinkering or no real optimization attempts, no notion of a stop rule.
anchors.3: Runs optimizations ad hoc with little differentiation between attempts and loose regard for the 8-experiment limit.
anchors.5: Stays within the budget, keeps distinct experiments, and stops with a passing implementation selected as fastest.
anchors.8: Allocates the budget deliberately across genuinely different optimization hypotheses, sequences them from highest expected payoff, and stops cleanly once diminishing returns or the cap is reached.
anchors.10: Runs a near-optimal search under the constraint: each experiment tests a distinct, well-motivated idea informed by prior results, redundant attempts are avoided, and the final choice is justified as the best latency-vs-parity trade-off within the spent budget.
